title: The digestive tract in order
blurb: Trace food from mouth to anus, name every segment in order, and say what each region does.
question: A swallowed capsule camera has just passed through the pyloric sphincter. Which three regions will it pass through, in order, before it reaches the cecum?

teach.body: Formally, the alimentary canal (GI tract) is the continuous muscular tube from mouth to anus through which food passes while it is digested and absorbed. In plain English: it is a one-way tube, and everything you swallow travels the same route. Organs that help digestion but never carry food, such as the liver and pancreas, are accessory organs, not part of the canal.

steps.label: Mouth
steps.sub: Chewing; saliva starts starch digestion; forms a bolus

steps.label: Esophagus
steps.sub: Peristalsis only: no digestion or absorption

steps.label: Stomach
steps.sub: Churns food with acid and pepsin into chyme

steps.label: Small intestine
steps.sub: Most chemical digestion and most absorption

steps.label: Large intestine
steps.sub: Absorbs water and electrolytes; forms feces

teach.caption: Valves and sphincters between regions keep traffic moving one way.
Note that the duodenum, the first part of the small intestine, curves right after the stomach, and the large intestine frames the coiled small intestine.
Accessory organs send secretions (saliva, bile, pancreatic juice) into the canal through ducts.

items: Ingestion: taking food into the mouth.
Propulsion: swallowing, then peristalsis (wave-like smooth-muscle contractions) pushes food along.
Mechanical digestion: chewing, stomach churning and segmentation break food into smaller pieces.
Chemical digestion: enzymes split large molecules into absorbable units.
Absorption: nutrients pass from the canal into blood or lymph.
Defecation: undigested residue leaves as feces.

teach.h: After the stomach: the intestines in order

steps.label: Duodenum
steps.sub: First, about 25 cm; receives bile and pancreatic juice

steps.label: Ileum
steps.sub: Absorbs vitamin B12 and bile salts; ends at ileocecal valve

teach.caption: Teal = small intestine (the longest part). Orange = large intestine (shorter, about 1.5 m, but wider).
Gut bacteria in the large intestine make vitamin K and some B vitamins and ferment fiber.

head: Sphincter or valve
Between
Job
rows: Lets in bile and pancreatic juice

teach.body: Priya, a nursing applicant, shadows a clinic where a patient swallows a capsule camera. It slides down the esophagus by peristalsis, passes the lower esophageal sphincter, and is churned in the stomach. Through the pyloric sphincter it enters the duodenum, then the jejunum, then the ileum. At the ileocecal valve it enters the cecum, climbs the ascending colon, crosses the transverse colon, descends, curves through the sigmoid colon and reaches the rectum.

teach.text: The duodenum, jejunum and ileum are all SMALL intestine; the cecum, colon and rectum are LARGE intestine. The appendix hangs from the cecum, not the sigmoid colon, and the esophagus neither digests nor absorbs.

items: Order: mouth, pharynx, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, anus.
Small intestine: duodenum, jejunum, ileum; most digestion and absorption.
Large intestine: cecum, ascending, transverse, descending and sigmoid colon, rectum, anal canal.
Liver, gallbladder, pancreas, salivary glands, teeth and tongue are accessory organs.
Peristalsis moves food; sphincters and valves control passage between regions.

summary: You can now list every region of the alimentary canal in order, separate canal organs from accessory organs, and name the sphincters between regions. You can also match each region to its main job, from peristalsis in the esophagus to water absorption in the large intestine.

A.q: Which sequence lists the parts of the small intestine in the order chyme passes through them?
A.why: Chyme leaves the stomach into the duodenum, then moves through the jejunum and finally the ileum, which ends at the ileocecal valve.

whyNot.0: The duodenum is first: it receives chyme straight from the pyloric sphincter.
whyNot.2: The ileum is the last segment, not the middle one; it joins the cecum.
whyNot.3: This is the reverse order, from the large intestine back toward the stomach.

A.q: Which of these structures is NOT part of the alimentary canal?
A.why: The gallbladder is an accessory organ: it stores bile and releases it into the duodenum, but food never passes through it.

whyNot.0: The jejunum is the middle segment of the small intestine, so food passes through it.
whyNot.1: The pharynx carries the swallowed bolus from the mouth to the esophagus.
whyNot.3: The sigmoid colon is the S-shaped last part of the colon, before the rectum.

A.q: Which statement about the esophagus is correct?
options: It propels food by peristalsis without digesting it
It begins protein digestion as pepsin mixes with the bolus
It absorbs water and some salts before the stomach
It starts starch digestion with its own amylase
A.why: The esophagus is a muscular tube that moves the bolus to the stomach by peristalsis. No digestion or absorption happens there.

whyNot.1: Pepsin works in the stomach, where chief cells release pepsinogen and acid activates it.
whyNot.2: The esophagus absorbs nothing; water is absorbed mainly in the intestines.
whyNot.3: Starch digestion starts in the mouth with salivary amylase; the esophagus makes no enzymes.

B.q: A capsule camera has just passed through the ileocecal valve. Which structure does it enter next?
B.why: The ileocecal valve opens from the ileum into the cecum, the pouch at the start of the large intestine.

whyNot.1: The ileum is the segment the camera has just left; the valve marks its end.
whyNot.2: The ascending colon comes after the cecum, not directly after the valve.
whyNot.3: The sigmoid colon is near the end of the colon, just before the rectum.

B.q: Which feature best explains why the small intestine absorbs far more nutrients than the stomach does?
options: Rugae that let it stretch as chyme arrives
A three-layer muscularis that churns chyme
Gut bacteria that break down fiber and make vitamin K
Villi and microvilli that enlarge its surface
B.why: Circular folds, villi and microvilli give the small intestine an enormous surface area for absorption, and its brush border carries enzymes.

whyNot.0: Rugae are folds of the stomach lining that allow it to expand; they do not boost absorption.
whyNot.1: The three muscle layers that churn chyme belong to the stomach and serve mechanical digestion.
whyNot.2: Vitamin K-producing bacteria live in the large intestine, not the small intestine.

B.q: What is the main function of the large intestine?
options: Absorbing most amino acids and monosaccharides
Emulsifying dietary fats for pancreatic lipase
Reabsorbing water and electrolytes to form feces
Secreting brush-border enzymes to finish digestion
B.why: The large intestine absorbs water and electrolytes, and forms and stores feces. It has no villi and no digestive enzymes of its own.

whyNot.0: Amino acids and monosaccharides are absorbed in the small intestine.
whyNot.1: Emulsifying fat is the job of bile, which acts in the duodenum.
whyNot.3: Brush-border enzymes belong to the small intestine's microvilli.

C.q: Darnell has surgery to remove most of his ileum. Absorption of which substances is most directly at risk?
options: Vitamin K made by gut bacteria
C.why: The ileum is the site where vitamin B12 (with intrinsic factor) and bile salts are absorbed.

whyNot.0: Vitamin K is made by bacteria in the large intestine, which remains in place.
whyNot.2: Glucose and amino acids are absorbed mainly in the jejunum, the main nutrient-absorbing segment.
whyNot.3: Water and electrolytes are recovered mainly by the large intestine.

C.q: Which sequence correctly traces the large intestine from the ileocecal valve toward the anus?
options: Cecum, ascending, transverse, descending, sigmoid colon, rectum
Cecum, descending, transverse, ascending, sigmoid colon, rectum
Cecum, ascending, transverse, sigmoid, descending colon, rectum
Ascending, cecum, transverse, descending, sigmoid colon, rectum
C.why: The large intestine runs cecum, ascending colon, transverse colon, descending colon, sigmoid colon, rectum, anal canal, anus.

whyNot.1: Ascending and descending are swapped: the colon rises first on the right, then descends on the left.
whyNot.2: The sigmoid colon follows the descending colon, not the other way around.
whyNot.3: The cecum comes first: it is the pouch the ileocecal valve opens into.

C.q: Which statement about the alimentary canal is CORRECT?
options: The jejunum is the first segment of the large intestine
The pyloric sphincter separates the esophagus and stomach
The duodenum receives chyme directly from the esophagus
The appendix hangs from the cecum of the large intestine
C.why: The appendix is attached to the cecum, the first part of the large intestine.

whyNot.0: The jejunum is the middle segment of the small intestine; the cecum begins the large intestine.
whyNot.1: The pyloric sphincter lies between the stomach and duodenum; the lower esophageal sphincter guards the stomach entrance.
whyNot.2: The duodenum receives chyme from the stomach through the pyloric sphincter.

reteach.title: A one-way disassembly line
reteach.question: Picture a factory conveyor that takes products apart instead of building them. Where does each station sit, and who are the outside suppliers?

blocks.body: The mouth is loading and first cutting. The esophagus is a plain conveyor: it moves goods and does no work on them. The stomach is the mixing tank. The small intestine is the main workshop where parts are finally split and shipped out to the body. The large intestine is the drying and packing area, and the rectum is the loading dock. The liver, gallbladder and pancreas are outside suppliers piping in chemicals; nothing on the belt passes through them.

steps.label: Main workshop
steps.sub: Duodenum, jejunum, ileum: digest and absorb

blocks.text: Suppliers are not stations: the gallbladder, liver and pancreas pipe secretions into the duodenum, but food never travels through them.

explain.body: The mouth chews food and saliva begins starch digestion, forming a bolus. The pharynx swallows it into the esophagus, a muscular tube that moves it by peristalsis only. The lower esophageal (cardiac) sphincter at its base opens into the stomach and limits reflux.

test.q: Which structure limits reflux of stomach acid into the esophagus?
test.why: The lower esophageal (cardiac) sphincter sits between the esophagus and stomach and limits reflux.

whyNot.0: The pyloric sphincter controls emptying of the stomach into the duodenum.
whyNot.1: The ileocecal valve lies between the ileum and the cecum.
whyNot.2: The hepatopancreatic sphincter controls the flow of bile and pancreatic juice into the duodenum.

explain.body: A J-shaped bag with rugae and three muscle layers that churn food into chyme. Parietal cells secrete hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor; chief cells secrete pepsinogen; mucous cells protect the lining. Little is absorbed here (some water, alcohol, aspirin). The pyloric sphincter releases chyme into the duodenum.

test.q: Which cells secrete hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor?
test.why: Parietal cells make hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor, which is needed later for vitamin B12 absorption in the ileum.

whyNot.0: Chief cells secrete pepsinogen, the inactive form of pepsin.
whyNot.2: Mucous cells secrete mucus that protects the stomach lining from acid.
whyNot.3: Pancreatic acinar cells make pancreatic juice, which carries bicarbonate (a base), not acid.

explain.body: The longest part of the canal and the site of most chemical digestion and most absorption, thanks to circular folds, villi and microvilli. The duodenum receives chyme plus bile and pancreatic juice, the jejunum absorbs most nutrients, and the ileum absorbs vitamin B12 and bile salts.

test.q: Which segment receives bile and pancreatic juice through the hepatopancreatic ampulla?
test.why: Bile and pancreatic juice enter the duodenum, where they neutralize acid chyme and continue digestion.

whyNot.0: The jejunum follows the duodenum and is the main site of nutrient absorption.
whyNot.1: The ileum absorbs vitamin B12 and bile salts; secretions enter higher up.
whyNot.3: The ascending colon is part of the large intestine, well past the point where these secretions enter.

explain.body: About 1.5 m long and wider than the small intestine. It runs cecum (with the appendix), ascending, transverse, descending and sigmoid colon, rectum and anal canal. It absorbs water and electrolytes and forms feces; its bacteria make vitamin K and some B vitamins and ferment fiber.

test.q: Bacteria living in which region produce vitamin K?
test.why: Gut bacteria in the large intestine (colon) make vitamin K and some B vitamins.

whyNot.1: The jejunum absorbs nutrients from the diet; it is not the home of the vitamin K-producing bacteria.
whyNot.2: The duodenum is where bile and pancreatic juice mix with chyme.
whyNot.3: Stomach acid kills most microbes, so it does not host vitamin K-producing bacteria.
